{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"FAQPage","mainEntity":[{"@type":"Question","name":"What is camera inspection?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Camera inspection uses a waterproof video camera mounted on a flexible cable to visually inspect the interior of septic system pipes, drain lines, and sometimes tank interiors. The camera transmits real-time video to a monitor, allowing technicians to see blockages, cracks, root intrusion, collapsed pipes, and other problems without digging. This diagnostic tool helps identify the exact location and nature of problems before expensive repairs begin."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"How much does camera inspection cost in Miami?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Camera inspection in Miami typically costs $200-$400 for basic drain line inspection, $300-$600 for complete septic system inspection, and $400-$800 for extended inspections of large properties or multiple lines. Get multiple estimates from licensed contractors to find competitive pricing while ensuring quality service."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"What problems can camera inspection detect?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Camera inspection can detect blockages, tree root intrusion, pipe cracks or breaks, collapsed pipes, improper connections, scale buildup, and other interior pipe problems. Cameras can also verify pipe condition, measure distances to problems, and document system condition for property transactions or repair planning. However, cameras can't detect problems outside pipes like drainfield saturation or soil issues."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"How long does camera inspection take?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Basic camera inspection typically takes 30-60 minutes, depending on the length of pipes inspected and complexity of access. Complete septic system inspections including tank and all drain lines can take 1-2 hours. Extended inspections of large properties or multiple systems may take 2-3 hours. Most contractors provide time estimates when scheduling."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Do I need a permit for camera inspection in Miami?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Routine camera inspection typically doesn't require a permit in Miami. However, if camera inspection is part of a larger repair, replacement, or system modification, Miami-Dade County DERM permits may be required. Your contractor can advise on permit requirements for your specific situation. Always work with licensed contractors who understand local permit requirements."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Can camera inspection replace other septic services?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Camera inspection is a diagnostic tool that complements but doesn't replace other septic services. While cameras can identify problems, they don't fix them - repairs still require appropriate services like pumping, cleaning, or pipe replacement. Camera inspection is most valuable when combined with comprehensive septic inspection and appropriate repairs based on findings."}}]}
